analysis:
Reviewed the two head_text units of docs/architecture/inference.md (lines 420-1216). The only change recorded in file_changes is a documentation-only edit at head lines 2966-2970, which is outside the supplied excerpts. It says the cluster control leader re-plans after an update only once both Macs report the same worker build (ClusterOnboardingUpdate.oneBuild), and it links the pair's coordinated update. It introduces no code, configuration, endpoint, key-handling or authorization change.

The supplied text is existing documentation for the Nemotron Super slot, prefix cache, MTP, logprobs and GLM5Next. It describes the encrypted SSD checkpoint store (SSDHybridCheckpointStore) with authenticated cache-scope partitioning, which matches the T-041 posture: scope is coordinator-authored, text prefix reuse is off without a scope, and image reuse is bound to a feature identity. It also describes fail-closed behavior: pinned shard SHA-256 checks, a load refused on aggregate-hash mismatch, and retained-native-fault charging. None of this prose conflicts with the canonical threat model. Because the edit sits outside the excerpts, I could not examine its surrounding paragraph. The oneBuild gating is a behavior claim in docs that I did not verify against source, and the referenced cluster-always-on.md was not supplied. The cluster re-planning and update coordination path may deserve review if cluster code changes elsewhere in the PR, but nothing here shows a security regression or an invalidated threat assumption. Remaining integration question: whether the cluster update and re-adoption code (ClusterService, ClusterOnboardingUpdate) changed in a way that affects trust or attestation across the two Macs.
